months.strategy:
The Dress Rehearsal.

Commercial job: Turn New Year intent into memberships that are active on 1 Feb, so every buyer walks into Stronger in 30 2.0 already in the habit. Re-up the 8 Jan-2026 annuals at list.

Newcomer: Week Zero, Hero (“Seven days unlimited for ₹1,999. Then 20% off if you stay.”). Speed is the lever: 60% of first-timers never return, and buyers who decide inside 72 hours stay longer. A 20% window that shrinks to 10% rewards the fast yes.

Newcomer: Resolution Insurance (“Keep your resolution and month two is 25% off.”). Only 34–40% of new clients buy a second time within 90 days. The bigger discount sits on purchase two and is earned by the attendance that predicts staying.

Newcomer: Kickstart 21: Opening Act (“21 coached days, then 20% off and straight into the challenge.”). Nervous January starters need a group, a coach and a finish line; graduation lands on challenge day one.

Winback: The Ex Factor (“Your ex wants you back. (It's us.) And it's paying 20% to say sorry.”). The challenge is members-only, so lapsed clients need a membership to join. A real 20% plus a deadline beats a reminder; the 3-month option lifts the ticket.

Renewal: Thirteen Is the New Twelve (“Your annual: 15% off, and the 13th month is on us.”). ₹12.5L of annuals come due in January. Losing one costs ₹1.9L; a 21% effective renewal keeps them and the cash upfront.

Renewal: Beat the Buzzer (“Renew before you expire, and go longer for less.”). Members whose plan lapses mid-challenge are the likeliest to drop. Rewarding early, longer renewals removes the gap and lifts cash per renewal 2.3–4.4×.
